long_biography.plain_text:
Bjäringer began at Alfred Berg in 1982 and spent nearly two decades in investment banking before moving to full-time capital allocation. His approach paired ownership with active governance: he backed businesses in sectors ranging from security services and fashion to enterprise software, often taking board roles alongside substantial stakes.

In 2012, he helped establish Monterro as a specialist buyer and developer of Nordic business-software companies. He has remained a significant shareholder in Björn Borg and serves on the board of Lasernet Group, formerly Formpipe. That combination of patient capital, corporate oversight and sector-focused investing has defined his career beyond any single transaction.
